correctness.rationale: For all \(m\ge3\), \(t\ge3\), and \(s_i\ge t\), the face constraints exactly identify deletion A and apex link B as joins of fixed-rank simplex skeleta. Each skeleton has an integral sphere-wedge type and canonical cycle lattice \(\bigwedge^r U\). The join dimensions differ by \(m\), so \(B\to A\) is nullhomotopic by connectivity and CW dimension. Thus the mapping cone is \(A\vee\Sigma B\) and no torsion occurs. The integral equivariant long exact sequence gives canonical top/bottom modules, with Koszul factor signs. Finite GF2 ranks and 360 signed Lefschetz checks independently corroborate examples without replacing the proof.
